simple.meaning: שִׁבְעָה (shibʻâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “seven (times).” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: שִׁבְעָה (H7655) appears 6 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Ezra 7:14, with occurrences in Ezra, Daniel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שִׁבְעָה (H7655) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in שִׁבְעָה (H7655) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: שִׁבְעָה (shibʻâh) / H7655 is traced through Ezra 7:14, Daniel 3:19, Daniel 4:13, Daniel 4:20 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Because you are sent by the king and his seven counselors, to inquire concerning Judah and Jerusalem, according to the law of your God which is in your hand,

timeline.evidenceText: Because you are sent by the king and his seven counselors, to inquire concerning Judah and Jerusalem, according to the law of your God which is in your hand,

Then Nebuchadnezzar was full of fury, and the form of his appearance was changed against Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. He spoke, and commanded that they should heat the furnace seven times more than it was usually heated.
“I saw in the visions of my head on my bed, and behold, a watcher and a holy one came down from the sky.
The tree that you saw, which grew, and was strong, whose height reached to the sky, and its sight to all the earth;
it is you, O king, that have grown and become strong; for your greatness has grown, and reaches to the sky, and your dominion to the end of the earth.
At the end of twelve months he was walking in the royal palace of Babylon.
